ud4.6:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud4.6:1.3: Then at that time venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja was sitting not far from the Fortunate One, after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, a forest-dweller, an alms gatherer, a rag-rober, one with (only) three-robes, with few longings, satisfied, completely secluded, unattached, with energy aroused, being one who spoke about the ascetic practices, (who was) applying (himself) to the higher mind.
ud4.6:2.1: The Fortunate One saw venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja, who was sitting not far away, after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, a forest-dweller, an alms gatherer, a rag-rober, one with (only) three-robes, with few longings, satisfied, completely secluded, unattached, with energy aroused, being one who spoke about the ascetic practices, (who was) applying (himself) to the higher mind.
ud4.6:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud4.6:4.2: ~ and restraint in regard to the Pātimokkha,
ud4.6:4.4: ~ and (living in) a remote dwelling place,
ud4.6:4.5: Being devoted to the higher mind ~ - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.”
